prompt: [Sentence Completion] Because the medieval town's charter exempted visiting merchants from the lord's road tolls, traders from three neighboring provinces ------- there, and within a generation its market had tripled in size.
explanation: 'Because' the charter removed the tolls, traders came together in the town, and the result clause ('its market had tripled in size') confirms that they gathered there in numbers: congregated.
distractor_rationales: malingered — pretending to be ill to avoid work would not make a market triple in size.
seceded — nothing in the sentence describes traders breaking away from a political body; they are drawn to a market.
perjured — nothing in the sentence involves a court or false testimony; the result is a market that grew.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] In order to ------- any appearance of favoritism, the judge withdrew from the case as soon as she learned that her former law partner was representing the defendant.
explanation: Withdrawing 'as soon as she learned' is a step taken in advance so that favoritism will never seem to arise: forestall means to prevent by acting first.
distractor_rationales: propagate — a judge would not step aside in order to spread an appearance of favoritism; withdrawing is meant to keep it from arising.
reconcile — there is no conflict between parties she is trying to settle; she is preventing an appearance.
substantiate — proving favoritism is the opposite of what withdrawing from the case aims at.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] The factory's owners had borrowed heavily to build a second plant just before demand collapsed, so when sales fell by half the company soon became ------- and could no longer pay its lenders.
explanation: Heavy borrowing plus halved sales leads to the stated result, 'could no longer pay its lenders' — the definition of insolvent.
distractor_rationales: complacent — the sentence describes debts and lost sales, not a self-satisfied attitude.
prestigious — collapsing sales and unpaid lenders do not raise a company's reputation.
autonomous — a company unable to pay its lenders becomes less independent, not more.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] To ------- the tight switchbacks on the mountain road, the bus line replaced its long coaches with shorter vans that could turn in a much smaller circle.
explanation: Vehicles that 'could turn in a much smaller circle' are chosen so the buses can travel through the bends successfully: to negotiate a road is to get through it.
distractor_rationales: circumvent — going around the switchbacks would not require vans that turn more tightly; tight turning is needed to drive them.
commemorate — nothing about honoring or remembering the road; the change is practical.
replicate — the bus line is not copying the switchbacks; it is driving them.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] Roman engineers laid their highways on deep beds of packed stone and dug drainage ditches along both sides; as a result, many stretches have proved so ------- that they still carry traffic two thousand years later.
explanation: The construction details lead, 'as a result,' to roads that 'still carry traffic two thousand years later' — that is, roads that last: enduring.
distractor_rationales: sinuous — stone beds and drainage ditches explain how long a road lasts, not whether it winds.
sumptuous — nothing about lavish cost or splendor follows from stone beds and ditches, and it would not explain the roads still carrying traffic.
derelict — roads that 'still carry traffic' are not abandoned or in ruins.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] So that they would never have to ------- with each other for passengers, the two airlines secretly divided the country's routes between them, an arrangement that regulators later ruled illegal.
explanation: Dividing the routes means each airline gets its own passengers, so the purpose is to avoid competing 'for passengers': vie.
distractor_rationales: dabble — one does not dabble 'with each other for passengers'; the purpose of splitting routes is to avoid competition, not casual involvement.
quibble — the arrangement removes rivalry 'for passengers,' not petty arguments between the firms.
tamper — dividing routes is not meant to stop the airlines from interfering with each other's equipment; the phrase 'for passengers' points to competition.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] Because the senator had voted against her own party on nearly every major bill that session, its leaders came to regard her as a -------, impossible to count on in any close vote.
explanation: Voting 'against her own party on nearly every major bill' and being 'impossible to count on' describe an independent who goes her own way: a maverick.
distractor_rationales: figurehead — a figurehead holds a title without real power; her votes clearly mattered to the leaders.
loyalist — a loyalist votes with the party, the opposite of what the sentence reports.
envoy — nothing in the sentence concerns representing a government abroad.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] To ------- their shaky claim to the throne, the new rulers commissioned genealogies tracing their family back to the ancient kings, though most of the ancestors listed had never existed.
explanation: Invented royal ancestors are meant to make a 'shaky claim' look lawful and rightful: legitimize.
distractor_rationales: relinquish — rulers giving up the throne would not invent royal ancestors to support their claim.
contest — they would not dispute their own claim; the genealogies are built to support it.
jeopardize — inventing ancestors to tie themselves to the ancient kings is meant to strengthen the claim, not endanger it.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] The village lies in a deep valley that the sun reaches for only a few hours each winter day, so its farmers coax only ------- harvests of potatoes and rye from the thin, cold soil, barely enough to feed the village until spring.
explanation: The cold, sunless valley and thin soil lead to harvests 'barely enough to feed the village' — yields just at the edge of sufficiency: marginal.
distractor_rationales: exotic — potatoes and rye are familiar staples, and the clue 'barely enough' concerns quantity, not unusualness.
perishable — 'barely enough to feed the village' describes how small the harvest is, not how quickly it spoils.
tropical — tropical harvests need heat, which is exactly what a sunless valley with cold soil lacks.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] To ------- shoppers who might otherwise wait for the holiday sales, the department store offered a free gift with every purchase made before November.
explanation: A free gift for buying early is a lure aimed at shoppers who 'might otherwise wait': entice means to attract with an offer.
distractor_rationales: appease — nothing suggests the shoppers are angry and need calming; they are simply waiting for sales.
exempt — a gift with purchase does not free shoppers from any rule or charge.
reimburse — the shoppers have not spent anything yet that the store would repay; the gift is an incentive to buy.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] The witness had changed her account of that night three times before the trial began, so the jury regarded her testimony as -------.
explanation: An account changed 'three times' gives the jury reason to doubt it: dubious.
distractor_rationales: unbiased — changing her story says nothing about her being free of prejudice; it undermines trust instead.
verbose — the clue is that the account kept changing, not that it was long-winded.
inaudible — whether the jury could hear her has nothing to do with her changing account.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] In order not to ------- the island's single freshwater spring, the council limits visitors to two hundred a month and turns away every cruise ship that asks to anchor in its harbor.
explanation: Limiting the number of visitors is a way of keeping demand on 'the single freshwater spring' below what it can supply, so the council acts so as not to overtax it.
distractor_rationales: desalinate — a freshwater spring has no salt to remove, and limiting visitors has nothing to do with that process.
monopolize — the council is keeping outsiders' demand low, not avoiding exclusive control of the spring by itself.
chlorinate — treating the water is unrelated to the number of visitors allowed on the island.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] Because the printing press let a single workshop turn out hundreds of identical copies in a week, books that had once been rare luxuries became ------- within a few generations.
explanation: The contrast with 'rare luxuries' and the cause (hundreds of copies a week) point to books becoming ordinary and widely available: commonplace.
distractor_rationales: unabridged — printing many copies says nothing about whether the texts were shortened.
illicit — mass production makes books more available, not illegal.
redacted — printing many copies does not black out parts of a text; the change described is from rare to plentiful.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] The framers divided authority among three branches of government so that no single branch could ------- the powers meant for the others.
explanation: Dividing authority 'so that no single branch could' take what is 'meant for the others' guards against seizing power wrongfully: usurp.
distractor_rationales: apportion — dividing powers among the branches is what the framers themselves did; it is not the danger they were guarding against.
ratify — approving the other branches' powers is not a threat that a separation of powers would be designed to prevent.
disavow — a branch renouncing other branches' powers would not endanger the balance; seizing them would.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] After a hard frost destroyed most of that year's coffee harvest, the beans that remained became so ------- that their price on world markets nearly doubled in a single season.
explanation: A frost that 'destroyed most of' the harvest leaves few beans, so each one becomes highly valued, and the doubled price confirms it: precious.
distractor_rationales: pungent — the frost reduced how many beans there were, not how strongly they smelled.
potent — nothing in the sentence concerns the beans' strength; the price rose because supply fell.
mellow — a milder flavor would not follow from the frost or explain a doubled price.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] Early mapmakers filled the unexplored interior of continents with sketches of elephants and sea monsters, a practice meant to ------- the empty regions that would otherwise have revealed how little they knew.
explanation: The drawings were 'meant to' hide the blank spaces that 'would otherwise have revealed' the mapmakers' ignorance: disguise.
distractor_rationales: fortify — sketches on a map do not strengthen the regions against attack; they hide the mapmakers' ignorance.
annex — drawing animals does not claim the land; the purpose is to keep the gaps from revealing ignorance.
partition — the sketches fill the regions rather than dividing them, and dividing would not hide how little was known.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] Since the contract had never been signed by either party, the court declared it ------- and refused to enforce any of its terms.
explanation: An unsigned contract that the court 'refused to enforce' has no legal force: void.
distractor_rationales: mutual — an agreement both sides had entered would be enforceable; this one was never signed by either party.
notarized — a notary certifies signatures, and this contract was never signed.
rigid — strict terms would still be enforced; the court refused to enforce any of them.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] To avoid ------- the powerful nobles, whose armies he still needed, the young king introduced his reforms gradually and credited each one to the advice of his council.
explanation: Moving 'gradually' and crediting his council are ways to keep from provoking nobles whose armies he 'still needed': antagonizing.
distractor_rationales: pardoning — the nobles have done nothing that needs forgiveness, and pardoning them would not be something to avoid.
outflanking — maneuvering around the nobles militarily is not what gradual reforms are designed to avoid.
enlisting — he 'still needed' their armies, so winning their support is something he wants, not avoids.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] The paper mill had been the town's only employer for sixty years, so when it closed, the local economy ------- and half the shops on Main Street were boarded up within two years.
explanation: Losing the 'only employer' leads to shops being 'boarded up' — the economy sank and failed: foundered.
distractor_rationales: prospered — boarded-up shops show decline, not success.
diversified — with the only employer gone and shops closing, no new range of businesses appeared.
industrialized — the closing of the town's one mill removes industry rather than adding it.

prompt: [Sentence Completion] To ------- voters who could not read, the election board printed a small picture of each candidate beside the candidate's name on the ballot.
explanation: Pictures on the ballot are added so that voters 'who could not read' can still vote: accommodate means to adjust to meet someone's needs.
distractor_rationales: disqualify — adding pictures helps these voters take part; it does not bar them.
enumerate — pictures beside names do not count the voters.
censure — nothing in the sentence involves officially criticizing the voters.
